summary: Patch stops the IndexError but only by bounds-guarding the `del`, which masks the real defect: `blocks`/`num_blocks` shrink during iteration while `rep_blocks` does not, so index `i` desyncs across the three parallel lists. When the guard skips a delete, the non-minimal block system stays in `blocks`, so `minimal_blocks()` can silently return a non-minimal result instead of crashing.

issues.description: Root cause is index misalignment: `del num_blocks[i], blocks[i]` uses a `rep_blocks` index against lists that are being shortened in-loop while `rep_blocks` is filtered only afterward via `to_remove`. Guarding `i < len(...)` suppresses the crash symptom but does not realign the lists — with multiple non-minimal block systems the guarded-out entries remain in `blocks`/`num_blocks`, desyncing them from the filtered `rep_blocks`. A proper fix collects removal indices and deletes from all three lists consistently after the loop.

Because the skipped deletions leave stale non-minimal entries, the fix may not fully resolve the issue: it converts a hard IndexError into a potentially incorrect (non-minimal) return value for inputs that trigger more than one deletion, which is worse than crashing for a math library.
No comment explaining why the bounds guard is needed, leaving the subtle list-desync trap undocumented for future maintainers.
